info.title: calimly Inventory Management & Card Issuance API
info.description: Multi-tenant inventory management and card issuance platform: card SKUs, physical card instances, stock, batch uploads, card-file generation, transfers, disposals, branch requests, and printing configuration. Every endpoint responds with the same envelope - { success, data, error } - on both success and failure; see each endpoint's response examples for the shape of 'error' on that path.

post.summary: Generates an encrypted `.dat` card file for a tenant and streams it back as a raw binary download. Because the response body is the file, the hand-off metadata the tenant needs (`fileMac`, `cardCount`, `expectedRowCount`) travels in the InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.CardFilesController.FileMacHeader, InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.CardFilesController.CardCountHeader, and InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.CardFilesController.ExpectedRowCountHeader response headers instead of a JSON body.
post.description:
The request body contains full PANs in the clear — the only endpoint in the platform
that accepts them. Callers must use TLS, and the file must be delivered to the tenant
over a channel at least as protected as the one it arrived on.


All-or-nothing: if any card fails validation the response is 422 and no file is
produced. The per-card reasons are in `error.validationErrors`, keyed by the
card's index in the request.

metadata previously returned in the JSON body.

post.summary:
Uploads an encrypted batch file of cards. Valid rows are imported (or update an
existing card on re-sight); invalid rows never fail the whole upload — they are
collected and returned as a failed-rows Excel report alongside the counts.

ExpectedRowCount.description:
Caller-declared row count, checked against the file's actual row count
(`BatchErrors.ExpectedRowCountMismatch` on mismatch).

rejection before this action runs. M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.InventoryController.Upload(ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Batches.BatchUploadRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) can additionally return this code
with the standard envelope (`Batch.ActorNotResolved`) when the caller has no
resolvable tenant context — e.g. a system-admin token, which this endpoint doesn't support.

actorNotResolved.summary: The caller has no resolvable tenant context — e.g. a system-admin token, which this endpoint doesn't support since there's no tenant to upload cards for. Distinct from the far more common empty-body case (no/invalid token), which the controller-level 401 covers.

error.message: The acting principal could not be resolved.

200.description:
The upload completed — importedCount/failedCount always sum to the file's row count.
Invalid rows never fail the whole upload; failureReportBase64 carries a failed-rows
Excel report (masked PANs only) when failedCount is greater than zero, and is null otherwise.

allImported.summary: Every row imported or updated successfully — no failed-rows report.

partialFailure.summary: Some rows failed (unknown product/branch, invalid PAN, etc.) — the whole upload still succeeds with 200; failed rows never fail the batch, they're collected into an Excel report instead.

rowCountMismatch.summary: The caller-declared ExpectedRowCount doesn't match the file's actual row count — the whole file is rejected before any row is processed.

error.message: Expected 500 rows but the file contains 487.

decryptionFailed.summary: The file could not be authenticated/decrypted — wrong key, or corrupted/tampered ciphertext (AES-GCM tag check failed). A whole-file failure, not a per-row one.

error.message: The file could not be decrypted. It may be corrupted or encrypted with the wrong key.

BranchRequestStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a branch stock request (ERD §4.1 column `RequestStatus`, extended by API §4.9 decisions Q-04/Q-05). Persisted as `TINYINT`. The first four values are the ERD's own numbering and keep their original meaning unchanged. Values 4–6 are appended (decision D-02) so a fresh migration never has to renumber an existing value — the same approach DomainLayer.Enums.TransactionStatus already took when it appended `PartiallyReceived = 3` and `Disposed = 4`. Status is never assigned ad hoc by application code except for the two terminal closures (DomainLayer.Enums.BranchRequestStatus.Refused, DomainLayer.Enums.BranchRequestStatus.Cancelled). Every other transition is produced by M:DomainLayer.Entities.BranchRequest.RecomputeStatus, a pure function of the line counters (decision D-03) — so the values below describe reachable states, not steps in a fixed sequence a caller is guaranteed to walk through one at a time. Correction, superseding an earlier (incorrect) note here: a confirm call can no longer move a request straight to DomainLayer.Enums.BranchRequestStatus.Fulfilled regardless of whether its lines are Known-way or Unknown-way — the Unknown-way Maker-Checker workflow means a confirm only stages transfers now, it never settles one, so DomainLayer.Entities.BranchRequestItem.ReceivedQuantity-driven crediting (and therefore DomainLayer.Enums.BranchRequestStatus.Fulfilled) always happens later, at a separate `receive` call on the generated transfer.

ConfirmTransferPlan.description:
One transfer to be generated by a confirm call. Source is specified per transfer, not per
line (decision Q-14) — a single product split across two sources becomes two transfers.

ApplicationLayer.DTOs.BranchRequests.ConfirmTransferPlan.Items deliberately reuses ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Transfers.CreateTransferLine rather than
ApplicationLayer.DTOs.BranchRequests.StockRequestLine: the shipped `TransferService`/`ITransferComposer`
requires explicit `ProductItemIds` for a Known-way line at create time, so the
confirm payload has to carry the same shape a direct transfer create does — the API
specification's `items[{productId, transactedQuantity}]` is insufficient on its own.

CreateBranchRequest.description:
Create payload (API Spec §4.5). TenantId is used only by a system-admin
caller to target a tenant; for a tenant caller it is ignored (the token's tenant is used).

tenantId.description:
Used only by a system-admin caller to target a tenant; for a tenant caller it is ignored
(the token's tenant is used), mirroring `CreateProductRequest.TenantId`. In practice
every write to this resource is system-admin-only (decision Q-09), so this is normally
how the target tenant is supplied.

CreatePrinterRequest.description:
Create payload for `POST /api/printers` (Printing Module Q-01/Q-09: system-admin
only). MaticaConfig is required when UsingPrinterType
is DomainLayer.Enums.UsingPrinterType.Matica and must be absent when it is
DomainLayer.Enums.UsingPrinterType.Evolis — Evolis needs no server-side machine configuration
(module requirement §1).

CreateProductRequest.description:
Create payload (API Spec §4.6). TenantId is used only by a system-admin
caller to target a tenant; for a tenant caller it is ignored (the token's tenant is used).

Matica / Evolis (Printing Module, phase 7) let a
system admin attach the product's print configuration in the same call — "the product and
its printing configuration should behave as a single aggregate." Supplying either one
requires a system-admin caller (decision Q-09, confirmed); a tenant caller supplying
either fails with `PrintingErrors.ProductPrintConfigOnlySystemAdmin`. A tenant caller
may still create a plain product with neither supplied — only the combined
product-plus-configuration action is admin-gated, not product creation itself. Exactly one
of the two, matching ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Products.CreateProductRequest.UsingPrinterType, is required when either is supplied —
enforced by `IProductPrintConfigComposer.ValidateAsync`, the same validation the
standalone `PUT /api/products/{id}/print-config` endpoint uses.

CreateStockRequest.description:

requests (decision Q-11 / D-08).

supplied. Supplying both is refused rather than resolved by precedence: guessing which the
caller meant risks destroying the wrong cards, and disposal cannot be undone.

reason.description: Why the cards were written off. Required, non-empty.

DisposeTransferRequest.description:

off everything the transfer still carries, in one step, without receiving any of it.

ReceiveTransferRequest.description:

rather than inferred.

together with that family's payload, switches it — the old configuration row is hard
deleted, not soft deleted, in the same transaction as the new row's insert.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description:
Authentication endpoints (API Spec §4.1), reconciled with the authoritative §2 model:
single account per tenant, minimal JWT claims, no roles/permissions/branch.

tags.name: Branch
tags.description:
Branch management endpoints (API Spec §4.5). Requires authentication: tenant callers manage
their own branches; a system admin manages any tenant's branches. Hard delete is not exposed.

tags.name: BranchRequests
tags.description:
Branch stock requests endpoints (API §4.9). Requires authentication. A tenant caller creates,
confirms, refuses, and cancels its own tenant's requests; a system admin has read-only access
across tenants (decision Q7) — create, confirm, refuse, and cancel all reject an admin token outright.

tags.name: CardDisposals
tags.description: Standalone card disposal endpoints (API §4.10, Addendum A). Writes off cards sitting at a branch — damaged, spoiled, or discontinued — outside of any transfer. Disposal that happens while settling a transfer is `TransactionsController`'s M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TransactionsController.Receive(System.Int64,ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Transfers.ReceiveTransferRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) and M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TransactionsController.Dispose(System.Int64,ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Transfers.DisposeTransferRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken), not this controller. Two resources share this controller under the common `api/inventory` prefix: writing a disposal is a card-level action (`cards/dispose`), while listing and reading disposals is its own resource (`disposals`). Routes are given in full on each action rather than composed from a single class-level prefix, since the two don't share a parent segment. Never available to a system admin — unlike `TransactionsController`, there is no read-only admin path here at all; disposal is a tenant-only concept end to end.

tags.name: CardFiles
tags.description: Card-file generation endpoint (Card File Generation, Phase 9.6). Restricted to the bootstrap system admin via InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Security.AuthorizationPolicies.SystemAdminOnly, following InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TenantsController's pattern. Deliberately a separate controller from InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.InventoryController: that one is class-level `[Authorize]` and acts for the calling tenant, this one is admin-only and acts on behalf of a tenant. Two authorization postures in one controller would be legal and confusing.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description:
Batch card-upload endpoint (API Spec §4.8, Batch Upload Phased Plan Phase 7). Requires
authentication; the uploading tenant is resolved from the caller's token by
ApplicationLayer.ServicesContracts.IBatchUploadService itself, not by this controller.

tags.name: InventoryHistory
tags.description:
Aggregated transaction history view (API §4.10). A reporting alias over the same data as
M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TransactionsController.GetAll(ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Transfers.TransferListFilter,System.Threading.CancellationToken) — same scope, same filter, same service call —
kept as its own thin controller rather than a second route on
InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TransactionsController so the two stay easy to tell apart in routing tables
and Swagger without either name implying it owns the other.

tags.name: Printers
tags.description:
Printer registry endpoints (ERD §6, Printing Module decisions Q-01/Q-09). Requires
authentication: tenant callers get read-only access, scoped to their own tenant; only a
system admin may create, update, delete, or restore a printer —
ApplicationLayer.ServicesContracts.IPrinterConfigurationService enforces this itself, not this controller,
matching the locked "[Authorize] only, no permission attributes" convention. Hard delete
is not exposed.

tags.name: PrintImages
tags.description:
Print-image endpoints (revision, "Print Images & Product Print Configuration" change
request). Upload, replace, and migration are system-admin only — reversed from the
original design, where only tenants could upload. Retrieval is open to both roles, scoped
to the caller's own tenant for a tenant caller. Every image is served through
M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.PrintImagesController.Get(System.Int64,System.Threading.CancellationToken); there is no public static-file path for this content any more.

tags.name: Product
tags.description:
Product (catalog) management endpoints (API Spec §4.6). Requires authentication: tenant callers
manage their own products; a system admin manages any tenant's products. Hard delete is not
exposed (consistent with the Branch/Tenant modules and the locked soft-delete-only decision).

tags.name: ProductItems
tags.description:
Product-item endpoints (API Spec §4.7). Requires authentication; tenant callers are scoped to
their own tenant. The update recomputes branch stock in the same transaction.

tags.name: ProductPrintConfig
tags.description:
Product print-configuration sub-resource endpoints (decision Q-07:
`GET`/`PUT /api/products/{id}/print-config`, no standalone POST/DELETE — the
configuration's create/delete lifecycle stays with the product itself, per the
single-aggregate design). Requires authentication: M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.ProductPrintConfigController.Get(System.Int64,System.Threading.CancellationToken) is tenant-scoped and
open to both roles; M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.ProductPrintConfigController.Update(System.Int64,ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Printing.UpdateProductPrintConfigRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken) is system-admin only (decision Q-09, confirmed) —
ApplicationLayer.ServicesContracts.IProductPrintConfigurationService enforces this itself, not this controller.

tags.name: Stock
tags.description:
Stock read endpoints (API Spec §4.7). Requires authentication; tenant callers see their own
tenant's stock across all branches, a system admin sees any tenant's stock.

tags.name: Tenants
tags.description:
Tenant management endpoints (API Spec §4.2). Restricted to the bootstrap system admin via
the InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Security.AuthorizationPolicies.SystemAdminOnly policy. Hard delete is intentionally
not exposed; only soft delete and restore are available.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description:
Card-transfer endpoints (API §4.10). Requires authentication. A tenant caller creates and
settles its own tenant's transfers; a system admin has read-only access across tenants
(decision Q7) — create, receive, and dispose all reject an admin token outright.


Every line — Known-way or Unknown-way — now follows the same create-then-settle shape
(Unknown-way Maker-Checker workflow): creating a transfer never finalizes stock movement by
itself, and every transfer opens `InProgress` until a separate M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TransactionsController.Receive(System.Int64,ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Transfers.ReceiveTransferRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
call states what was actually confirmed. The same account may create and later settle a
transfer — both identities are recorded on the transfer regardless (see
`TransferDetailResponse.CreatedByUsername`/`CheckedByUsername`).


There is no separate refuse endpoint. Every settlement outcome — received, disposed, or
(for whatever is left over) returned — goes through M:InventoryManagmentAndInstanceIssuancePresentationLayer.Controllers.TransactionsController.Receive(System.Int64,ApplicationLayer.DTOs.Transfers.ReceiveTransferRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken), which carries a
disposition per product line: an explicit per-card outcome for a Known-way line, or a
received quantity plus (when there's a remainder) a difference action for an Unknown-way
line. An Unknown-way line cannot be disposed of — it moves entitlement only, so there is no
physical card to write off.
